digests.headline: Alonso's Chelsea takes shape: a record fee, a £52m defender and Villa's set-piece brain

week.text: Morgan Rogers arrives from Aston Villa for £117m — the biggest fee ever paid by an English club — with Alejandro Garnacho heading the other way on a loan primed to turn permanent. Xabi Alonso has his marquee signing.

Maxence Lacroix passed his medical in London as the £52m deal with Crystal Palace completed this week, per Romano. The Athletic's verdict: his experience and physicality are exactly what this defence needs.

Chelsea triggered Austin MacPhee's release clause and he's said his goodbyes at Villa Park. Under him, Villa out-scored every top-five-league side from set-pieces in 2023–24 — the sharpest quiet signing of the summer.
Talks are live with Leverkusen for Kerim Alajbegović, but Romano insists there's no £34m bid — Chelsea's ceiling is under €30m and Italian clubs are still circling. A fee standoff, not a done deal.
Como's third bid of around £26m is close to Chelsea's £30m-plus-add-ons ask, per Ben Jacobs, with talks set to accelerate over the weekend.

team_watch.name: Morgan Rogers
team_watch.note: The English-record buy. The Guardian's club-by-club guide calls him the capture to excite supporters — while noting a top centre-back and striker are still craved.

team_watch.name: Emmanuel Emegha
team_watch.note: Expected back in time for the Premier League opener but will likely miss the overseas pre-season tour, per Nizaar Kinsella.

team_watch.name: Mike Penders
team_watch.note: The Guardian reads Chelsea's reluctance to sign a keeper as a sign Penders isn't far from competing for the No 1 shirt.

team_watch.name: Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli
team_watch.note: Included in the pre-season tour squad at 16 — r/chelseafc approves.

digests.today: No Chelsea football today — the pre-season opener against Juventus at the Bridge is still eleven days out, so tonight's kick-offs are other people's friendlies: Palace at Bromley, Celtic–Milan, and Juventus in Liège near midnight IST. The real action is on the phones: Como's talks for Chalobah accelerate this weekend and the Alajbegović haggling with Leverkusen rolls on. A perfectly good night to close the app and let the sporting directors earn their salaries.

wider.title: Premier League: club-by-club guide to transfer business so far – and what they still need
wider.hook: Where all 20 clubs actually stand, in one read — including the honest ledger on Chelsea: Rogers, Palestra, Quenda and Emegha in; Cucurella, Santos and George out.

wider.title: Chelsea have spent ~£1.8bn. I built a spreadsheet showing why that's not the whole PSR story.
wider.hook: A fan actually did the amortisation maths on the £1.8bn — and the comment thread arguing over it is the real value here.

wider.title: Como becomes the first club to ban headers in their youth academy following guidance from Raphael Varane
wider.hook: Varane retired citing the damage heading did to him; now a Serie A club is acting on it. The community-voted story of the day, and the debate underneath is worth your time.

read.title: 'You need to evolve': Enzo Maresca plots life after Pep at Manchester City
read.hook: Chelsea's former manager now has the least enviable job in football: following Guardiola. Opens with a tribute to Kevin Keegan and reaches for the Ferguson and Wenger successions — worth it for those parallels alone.

rivals.note: The champions aren't hunting a No 9 for once — but they missed out on Rogers to Chelsea and won't want to lose the Alex Scott race too.
The Maresca era begins with a £116m Elliot Anderson and the small matter of following Guardiola — Chelsea fans know how his second seasons go.
Took Andrey Santos off Chelsea's hands for £50m and he's already knitting their midfield together with Mount — a sale that could age either way.
Iraola is backing his backroom staff to cure their set-piece ills — the week Chelsea bought the best set-piece coach in the league.
